title: AI Talking Avatar: Make Any Character Speak
summary: Make an AI talking avatar from one picture: add a line as text or audio and Flick makes the face speak it in sync. See 19 real talking clips. Start free.
body_markdown:
### What is an AI talking avatar?


An AI talking avatar is a video made from a still picture of a person or character, where the face speaks a line with lip movement that matches the words. In Flick you make one with Character Dialogue from a picture and an audio line, or with Image to Video from a picture and a typed line.


### Can I make a photo talk with AI for free?


Yes, you can start free: Text to Voice with Eleven v3 and Image to Video with MiniMax H3 Max, which makes video with synchronized audio, are on the Free plan. You get 100 credits when you sign up and 100 credits every week, while Character Dialogue needs the Standard plan at $20 a month.


### How do I make an AI avatar talk in my own voice?


Record the line yourself, upload it as an mp3, wav, m4a, ogg or aac file, and attach it as the Audio in Character Dialogue next to your picture. The avatar then speaks with your exact timing and voice.


### How does AI lip sync work for a talking avatar?


Character Dialogue moves the mouth and face to the sound of the audio you give it, so the timing comes from your recording. Image to Video models such as Seedance 2.0 make the voice and the mouth together from the words quoted in the prompt.


### Should I use Character Dialogue or Image to Video for a talking avatar?


Use Character Dialogue when the line is already recorded and must stay exact, and Image to Video when you want the camera, the body and the voice made with the shot. Ulysses, a short made in Flick by Jaime Yao, uses both.


### Can I make a photo of a real person talk?


Only with that person's permission, and never to put words in their mouth that they did not say or would not agree to.


### Who owns the talking avatar videos I make?


You do. Content you generate on Flick is yours for personal and commercial projects. See the terms of use for detail.
